thesis: The book argues for relational realism: beauty is real in encounters among worldly properties, capacities and conditions, without a universal ranking.

ideas.statement: Observer dependence is not arbitrariness; cultivated taste identifies properties, corrects facts and compares perspectives while permitting justified disagreement.

evidenceAndExamples.statement: Suitable conditions can become circular; an ideal observer stripped of vulnerability may lose part of the phenomenon rather than reveal one final taste.

objectionsAndQualifications.statement: Suitable conditions can become circular; an ideal observer stripped of vulnerability may lose part of the phenomenon rather than reveal one final taste.

audit.notes: Direct active-LLM analysis; argument distinguished from established empirical result.
